content.text:
## IO Limiters (20-Year Anniversary Edition) \[[Free DL](https://sanjayaprime.bandcamp.com/album/io-limiters-20-year-anniversary-edition)\]

I stand here amidst the ghosts of the dead. IO Limiters: 20th Anniversary Edition is not a remaster -- it's a resurrection. Two decades after the original release, I have completely rewritten and re-orchestrated every track from the ground up, transforming the original vision into a progressive audiographic journey that spans atmospheric trip-hop, haunted breakbeat, and glitchcore. As the sole surviving member of our original collective, this album serves as a testament to the passing of time and a memorial to our fallen: the late Mushuto, who first brought me to Trochlear Recordings, and Supa, the Ghostface Geisha. Even Mojo's Coffee in Austin, where most the original album was produced, is now lost and lives on only in legend. From the dark carnival brokenbeat of "Sombranoche" to the IDM-infused nostalgia of "Remembrance," these songs carry the weight of twenty years of scars, tattoos, and untold stories.

The album is structured as a temporal triptych -- Yesterday, Today, and Tomorrow -- exploring the entropy of our simulation. It moves from the reverse-engineered bittersweet piano of the past, through the psybient "Liminal" spaces of the present, and into a future where silica replaces carbon. I embrace this evolution. We were always -- _always!_ -- the torchbearers; never the torch. In that vein, the production evolves from organic orchestration to the highly technical xMaqina remix of "Teqnofobia". This is a story of pain chosen, oceans left behind, and the math finally adding up -- a definitive expansion of the IO universe.

While I had BMFD to master the original, this time around I'm going by my sight alone as my hearing has only continued to degrade over the years. Technology's come a long way, and what my eyes and ears can't account for, the machines have had to make up for those weaknesses. It's not perfect.

But I'm no longer interested in perfection.

content.text:
## ./NFO{"Reflections on the Dead"}

With ghosts, its always important to remember to never let the past detract from those who still draw breath in the present.

_Pretty words. Sounds good on paper._ Doesn't change the difficulty level to adapt to those words for those of us who are haunted.

Mushuto along with my brother Skybreak know the most about the foundation of this series and the album that started it all. My sister Gaea, as well. IO, input/output, a 1 and a 0 -- Yin and Yang -- because we cannot know with even an iota of certainty that there really _is_ a world beyond our senses.

In studying myself, especially in the filters by which I define and "accept" my reality, I found potential weaknesses, ways by which I limit reality. Every limiter causes loss in clarity. Some we cannot currently overcome, not with our present state of sensational capabilities. To take merely our eyes, they show us only 0.0035% of the electromagnetic spectrum, meaning we're blind to more than 99% of all is around us (99.997% to be exact).

But psychological and emotional limiters? Those I _could_ work with... and, in doing so, open up new planes of existence by overcoming them. By identifying and working on these limiters within myself, I began to see how they operated within others around me. All but one of these I have overcome and made a part of myself. And no, I won't be disclosing which one of those remains.

*   **La Manera del Dolor (aka, "Sorrow's Path")**: Humans are not the only Terran fauna to hold onto their pain. It's quite common, as it can prevent repeating that which took us to that point of pain. But we're one of the only creatures to romanticize it, to wear it as a badge of honor, to hold it nearer -- sometimes even above all other sensations -- I would go so far as to say some of us "treasure" it. It is... _precious to us_. I found this limiter in myself and found that it held me back from exploring, from diving into the darkness, even to shy away from enjoyment or the "lighter" side of what we call reality.
*   **IO (Yesterday)**: That which came before. Not fear of the past, not being locked into the past so that it destroys your future. No, those are limiters within the psychic cages of others. For me it is the desire to return, to live previous worlds anew and here in this life. To see it all torn down and replace with what-once-was.
*   **Sombranoche (aka, "Nightshade")**: Atropa belladonna (aka, "Nightshade") entrances me. It introduced me to the idea that a poison can also be a medicine. In fact, snake venom itself is what's used to create anti-venom. The secret is in the dose. Where do we see a poison and can't look past it to find its power? The answer turned out to be rather unbelievable. Nearly every weakness, no matter how disabling, can be turned into a strength.
*   **Time Interrupt**: I suffer from a rare disease called "paradox syndrome" which, especially near the turn of the millennium, was quite disruptive to my acceptance of the reality in which we currently reside. Part of it is due to the past memories from other lives, which is jarring to be reminded of by a simple smell, then realize _that_ smell is likely the only surviving remnant of that time. That's the smallest part of it. The larger part is that I tri-associate memories. The side effect of this is that every time a part of our nested simulation is rewritten -- or, worse, reset entirely -- for some reason I remember the parts that were erased. In very rare circumstances, recalling these memories actually helps, such as when my brother Zero and I first entered Emiliano Zapata, Mexico, and the color of the clay alongside the river triggered one of those memories. I turned to Zero, saying, "We can put down the maps. I know where we are." _That_, however, is an example of an exception. Most the time it just distracts from "the reality we have" and tries to pull my mind towards other times and realities.
*   **IO (Today)**: I'm a futurist by default. Enjoying today, even accepting now -- _the moment!_ -- requires effort and conscious awareness. Did I just release a new album? Win an award? Get featured in another magazine? _Too bad! time to get back to creating._ In the five years I spent as a monk, one of those years was studying under the tutelage of Ganesha. My name "Jaya" grew to become my primary entity and identity during this time, with one of my lessons to learn what it truly means to wear the name "Victory" itself. One of the articles I read during that time was from Scott Adams, talking about "champagne moments" and the importance of celebrating major milestones. Stop. Pause. Here in this moment -- _now!_ -- Celebrate what you've accomplished. Savor it. Let it in. Don't pass go, DO collect $200 dollars. Tomorrow isn't your time; it's today.
*   **Depthcharm**: A few know that I was once afraid of water. It would be a surprise to others, as I'm a veritable fish who will stay on the waves for hours. It's not the fear of swimming in water, nor drowning... in fact, drowning comes with its own sweet lullaby. No, it was the fear of falling asleep near the sound of the ocean's waves. I've never been able to explain the fear nor pinpoint the source of it, but I truly believed at the time that -- should I fall asleep within earshot of the waves -- the ocean would pull me under and into a sleep from which I'd never wake up. Maybe one day she will. Maybe she's merely waiting until the time is right. If so, then I welcome that moment when it arrives.
*   **Liminal**: Always starting, always "in between"; never finished... never... _complete_. This was the very first limiter I found in my psyche, the first crack in the idea that I was a perfect, complete creation... and that any error or break in my own code was due to external sources. Even as I write this, I'm pulled back in time by my memory. The world is passing by, drifting by, from my passenger seat in Wolf Willie's van -- my blood father. We have the windows cracked, causing the 200 or 300 post-it notes he's pasted all over the dashboard to flutter in the breeze. Every one of the notes is an idea -- a lyric, a song concept, a drawing idea -- fluttering and fragile, as if any moment they could be pulled away by the wind. So many dreams on the very brink of being forgotten. _And now that he's dead?_ Where then did those dreams go? All the creations I'd started and never finished, they never really go away. They haunt me, filling my internal Task Manager, even in the background. There's no way to empty it completely, to finish everything. There's always more. But completing even one frees up that space... opening that new void to fill with others.
*   **Teqnofobia**: My proof that I have surpassed this limiter is that technologists see me as a luddite, while technophobes see me as a futurist. I still hold a healthy skepticism of technology, and yet celebrate and revel in the memetic advances across the planet in this very same moment. My skepticism let's me doubt and test each advance, finding the cracks, as well as the ways to improve on them. My futurism gives me the vision to see how each advance is merely a stepping stone... sometimes even the ability to step back and away from it all... to see the wall itself in which each advancement forms the stones.
*   **Source of Warmth**: It's not just an addiction to violence, to fighting, but truly a "comfort in strife" that means whenever the waters are calm... that never, ever should those waters be trusted. _The only calm is the calm before a storm!_ To me, the image that comes with this song is that of a nuclear bomb going off, and feeling myself hold out my hands to warm myself by its fire... _a moth to the final flame_. The original album began with this song, where now it takes its rightful place on the verge of tomorrow.
*   **Mi Tigrita**: My drummer, BMFD, once said, _"Your fucking sonar ping for train wrecks spans the size of Texas!"_ It's true. I don't just have an unhealthy attraction to deep fried Twinkies, but I can sniff 'em out. I'm drawn to them. I have a love for violent, dangerous women. Other women that The Average Joe would annoyingly call "a ten" don't do it for me. _Got a million followers on Instagram with your entire life planned out perfectly? I don't care. Call me when you pick up a heroin addiction. Maybe then I'll let you try out that taser in your purse. A'ite, Hot Pocket? Snort a few lines, get wasted, then drunk dial my ass. We'll fucking go crash a car together!_
*   **IO (Tomorrow)**: It's one thing to predict the future -- to check the math and confirm the solution. It's another thing to live it. The first jarring realization was Google's "Deep Dreams" and, while the rest of the world was laughing at dog heads coming out of meatballs, I was the one trying to explain to everyone what they'd just done, _"Don't you see? They've given the machine memories. It's creating from its memories!"_ Then Google's Deep Mind released their paper on transistors and transformers within neural networks. At least a few were listening at that point. As I write this, it's 2026, July 12. We're living on the very verge of tomorrow, with every day confirming the math behind another equation. That doesn't mean we shouldn't still experiment... nor still run the numbers... it doesn't mean we're always right. One false calculation, one misplaced X instead of a Y, and we could lose everything.
*   **Remembrance**: The separation between the my solo productions and those we've performed live as a group is never more apparent than with "Remembrance" -- which, to this day, is the song we get asked most about in a live setting... and yet it's one of my three oldest creations. Most of the time when we play "Come One, Come All" on stage, we use a more jazzy version of "Remembrance" as the backdrop, such as on the "[Warriors in Waiting](warriors-in-waiting-live-set)" live set. I won't detail this one with my own words. Instead, I'll share this poem.

content.html:
"Piano" by D H Lawrence

Softly, in the dusk, a woman is singing to me;
Taking me back down the vista of years, till I see
A child sitting under the piano, in the boom of the tingling strings
And pressing the small, poised feet of a mother who smiles as she sings.

In spite of myself, the insidious mastery of song
Betrays me back, till the heart of me weeps to belong
To the old Sunday evenings at home, with winter outside
And hymns in the cosy parlour, the tinkling piano our guide.

So now it is vain for the singer to burst into clamour
With the great black piano appassionato. The glamour
Of childish days is upon me, my manhood is cast
Down in the flood of remembrance, I weep like a child for the past.

content.text:
## ./NFO{"Audiographic Detailing"}

On the production side, this album has been 20-years in the making, with live versions for many of these evolving so much over the years as to become nearly unrecognizable. When detailing the audio itself here below, I'll simply copy over my journals as I neared completion for each one of these.

1.  **La Manera del Dolor**: "Sorrow's Path" -- now the haunting, spectrum-building "La Manera del Dolor" -- was originally birthed to carry my live poem "Transient Charm," an experiment we scrapped after it spectacularly derailed twice. My apologies to any who were there in the audience that bore witness to those failures. If this track doesn't hook you, do yourself a favor and walk away from the rest of the album right now. I drew heavy blood from the original cut, but mad love to anyone who can spot the 80s fantasy film I straight jacked the chord progression from. The current cover art rides a wave inspired by Cory and Catska Ench's 2008 Burning Man poster—a fitting nod to the thirteen years I've spent out in that dust—but I'll likely weave some of my own digital fractals into the final piece before January hits. The track itself is mostly locked, save for one possible tweak... we'll just have to see where the winds take it before launch.
2.  **IO (Yesterday)**: I knew right from the jump that "IO" -- the album's title track -- had to be sliced into three acts just like the original story: _Yesterday_, _Today_, and _Tomorrow_. It's both beautiful and horrifying to finally be living in a reality where Today has actually become Tomorrow. A month ago, I was painfully layering the beats for "Yesterday" in Audacity, brute-forcing it without a proper sequencer -- a brutal handicap I've since fixed. I was 90% locked, just missing a few fades and instrumental layers, when Johnny Boy took his exit strategy. That knocked the wind right out of me, so I abandoned the session and pivoted to the iPad and piano to bleed out the new version of "La Manera del Dolor." When that track neared readiness, I finally faced the unfinished "IO" still waiting in Audacity, catching an immediate, undeniable impulse to breathe a gentle, low-reed flute into those empty spaces -- while leaving the original samples exactly where they belong.
3.  **Sombranoche**: Mushuto didn't even ink my name to Trochlear Recordings until he caught that very first rough draft of "Sombranoche" (aka "Nightshade"). It's a track built on the fear of the unknown -- a harsh reminder that anti-venom is distilled straight from the venom itself. With Mushuto and Supa gone, leaving only their tracks behind, I'm left wondering if it's even still a record label when I'm the sole survivor acting as caretaker to the ghosts. When I cracked open the sessions to resurrect _IO Limiters_ for this twenty-year anniversary run, it was only right that "Sombranoche" led the charge. It's fully production-ready now alongside "Source of Warmth," while the bones of "La Manera del Dolor" are finally locking into place. The real danger with "Nightshade" was straying too far off the trail, but I finally wrangled that original dark essence back into the mix. If I can get this iPad fixed up over the weekend, I'll be tearing into the rest of the roster. Not every old track is surviving the cut, but the heavy-hitters are already on deck.
4.  **Time Interrupt**: This one rides closer to its original cut than anything else on the roster, but I've still dragged it through the dirt to inject some deep, gut-punching bass and heavy electro elements. In full disclosure, my time spent remixing Daft Punk (aka "[TH3 GR1D](daft-punk-the-grid-remix)") -- and soaking in their absolute masterclass in orchestration -- is what really drove the evolution of this track. It's one of the rare straight-up 4x4 bangers on the album, a relentless pulse that perfectly mirrors that broken, glitchy passage of time as the sound mutates from one level to the next.
5.  **IO (Today)**: This new cut is my absolute first stab at a breakcore track, and honestly, it might just be my last. The piano lays down a solid anchor while the beats and sound effects go completely off the rails, perfectly mirroring the slippery, chaotic nature of "the moment" itself—and all that heavy static we have to punch through just to find a scrap of clarity. To wrangle that madness, I had to drag the whole session down to an agonizing crawl, slowing the piano and organically hammering out the rhythm on an MPC before painting that final layer of erratic sound effects over the wreckage.
6.  **Depthcharm**: This limiter once had me by the throat -- that terrifying, hypnotic pull back to an unreachable life beneath the waves. It was so intense I couldn't even sleep near the ocean, paranoid the sound alone would drag my soul out to sea and I'd never wake up. I finally broke that curse a year after '04 by squatting on the coastline for weeks, straight-up daring the water to take me. She didn't, and while I still love the ocean, those sirens don't own me anymore. The track mirrors that exact evolution; the first half bleeds heavy from my 2006 cut of "Depthcharm" before mutating into an aggressively droning beast, deeply haunted by the late great Manu Shrine's "Betrayed" and keeping Sergey right there in my chest while I navigated the mix. I've even been weaponizing Meta's new Segment Anything audio AI to rip underwater YouTube recordings, meticulously mapping out where every dolphin and whale echoes across the soundscape. I'm giving it a few final spins to plug the last gaps, but after years of obsessive tinkering, I'm hitting that wall where I'm going completely deaf to the layers -- which means it's just about time to lock it down. You can check out some of the 3D stereoscopic layering [here on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IVrRXlXIJNs).
7.  **Liminal**: We're bleeding into the final stretch of the IO Limiters 20-Year Anniversary cut -- just a handful of mastering tweaks and brutal re-cuts left before the whole thing is locked down. We're closing out these previews with "Liminal," a track that lives exactly on that bleeding edge between the past and what comes next. It kicks off with the classic bones of the original before dragging you through some heavy EDM and dubstep trenches, but the real trip hits in the back half. That's where I take my very first raw dive into straight-up psytrance, paying a massive nod to those days two decades ago when Shpongle and Ott completely hijacked the Goa scene. The final minutes just shred the high ends, filtering and echoing them through absolute distortion until the whole track crosses the threshold. It perfectly embodies its namesake, and hands down, it's my absolute favorite cut on the entire record.
8.  **Teqnofobia**: This is easily the most SFX-heavy beast on the roster, pulling in a chaotic collision of samples produced by Red Rock, raw cuts recorded by Teron Solus, and a heavy dose of my own sonic madness. It's wild to realize just how many of my other tracks were actually birthed right out of this single song's DNA -- crawling straight outta the noise, the distortion, and the relentless grinding of some endless factory floor. The trick wasn't just making it heavy; the real challenge was wrestling all that brutal, mechanical chaos into something you could actually comprehend without your brain completely short-circuiting.
9.  **Source of Warmth**: The original 2006 cut used to kick down the door as the album's opener, detonating at the exact second the bombs dropped. Two decades later, I've flipped the script for this remaster. Tt now serves as the heavy-hitting closer for the album's "Today" section. I dragged a ton of organic, natural drums into the mix this time around, stacking them hard over a crushing bassline laced with grimy dubstep strikes. But even with all that added weight bearing down, if you listen close beneath the wreckage, you can still feel that same haunted, Japanese jungle pulse bleeding through from the original.
10.  **Mi Tigrita**: This cut is pure, intentional self-sabotage. I'm burying "Mi Tigrita" at the absolute bitter end of the album, forcing you to survive the heavy gauntlets of "Technophobia" and "Source of Warmth" just to earn the right to hear it. It's a bullet to the track's play count, but the survivors are rewarded with the final holy trinity: "IO (Tomorrow)," this track, and "Remembrance." Out of all the remakes, this rides closest to the original bone -- stripped to its rawest mechanical gears before violently mutating at the midway point. It's driven by my favorite instrument, the cold yet strikingly human music box, echoing the haunted ballerina from my "In Heaven" fever dreams. Fittingly, this is also the exact track we play live to carry my poem, "Transient Charm" (see "[Warriors in Waiting](warriors-in-waiting-live-set)").
11.  **IO (Tomorrow)**: What does it sound like when the smoke finally clears? To me, it's sweeping arps and distant chimes echoing that original harmony, all anchored down by a heavy, deep-rolling bassline. "Tomorrow" -- the final cut of the core "IO" trinity -- is officially locked, capturing a tomorrow-day that is rapidly bleeding right into our today-today. It's easily my favorite of the three, hitting so hard that I actually flirted with dropping a standalone "IO" EP just to carve out a few more experimental mixes. That's a long shot at this point... but nothing is ever truly impossible.
12.  **Remembrance**: This cut is the absolute hinge where my live crowd and studio junkies finally collide. We tried bleeding my live poem "Come On, Come All" over a handful of different beats such as "Sombranoche" and "La Manera del Dolor", but this track easily took the throne as our mainstay -- stripping the chaos down to isolated guitar riffs, heavy bass chords, and jazz-soaked piano progressions for the stage. The track's entire lifeblood is weaponized nostalgia; it’s engineered to drag absolutely anyone, anywhere, backward into a moment that's still calling their name. Namen actually caught this live with Jaime of all people, way back at our very first group gig for the Mojo's Coffee House Solstice Party. After all the blood, sweat, and broken years, I truly believe this new cut finally does justice to both the raw original and this massive twenty-year milestone.

texts: "There never was a way. A hundred paths of pain. Forever draws me near. Release the reigns of fear."

content.text: ## Scorched Earth -- Raze the Past With this 20-year edition temporarily perfected, what then of the original? The original carries within it the samples that Red Rock and I made on his Micron, recordings that I captured while hitchhiking, even production tips and suggestions from Mushuto -- who helped guide my original album. The only song I even listen to anymore on that OG version is "Remembrance" and... well.. . I'm not sure I'll even be listening to _that_ anymore. My sister Gaea and I have stood together around burn barrels, their flames flickering into the night and warming us in the desert at Burning Man. Together we've made a ritual of sacrificing journals that no longer serve us to the flames. That brings me to the question: do I keep the original "IO Limiters" as a foundation stone? Or do I allow the "Spirit of Ares" to consign it to the flames? I will leave those originals for others. For now. Perhaps a measure of what once was, relative to what now is, will in fact prove useful... if not to myself, then to others. ## Apocalypse -- The End While it didn't officially drop until January of 2006, the blood and sweat for my first album of original music was already spilling out right around this time in '05. I was holed up at Mojo's Coffee House down in Austin -- an absolute legend of a spot in the "third space" -- grinding alongside Mushuto (also an absolute legend), who was somehow juggling three albums of his own at the exact same time. I was effectively living out of Mojo's for those months. I'd post up for two days straight before even thinking about stepping outside to catch a breather. Then came the "unending week." Mushuto and I spent seven days straight at Mojo's building our record label from the ground up. You remember MySpace, right? Hell yes, we got all our artists wired into MySpace. Some of those relics actually still exist today, my own included. We were literally chained to that coffee shop 24 hours a day -- manufacturing tracks, swapping sounds, coding pages, passing out on the sofas in the back corner, and smoking the absolute fuck out of a million cigarettes! Fueled by nothing but each other's raw creativity along with lethal doses of caffeine 'n nicotine, we made more progress in a single week than we had in the previous six months combined. Right after Christmas, I was behind the decks for Naman's birthday. I dropped Sarah Slean's cover of "Climbing Up the Walls," and I've never seen that man leap over a counter so damn fast. Those are the exact moments behind the tables that I fucking L-I-V-E for! Right around then, Katie Bug came rolling into the ATX. Everyone was gearing up for the massive New Year's Eve blowout at Mojo's... because it was the last night their doors would ever be open. We even had Loki and the Marines all up in it. If you've ever seen the original cover art for IO Limiters, that photo came straight out of that unending week. Mushuto snapped it right there in Mojo's on that back sofa. I had just wrapped up the album the day before and was busy mixing down an adHF "[ADHD Revolution](adhd-revolution)" track to launch for NYE. When the clock struck midnight on New Year's Eve, Kevin -- one of the owners -- straight-up pulled the cash register out of the counter, locked it in his briefcase, and started dropping boxes of champagne all over the shop. "We're closed!" he yelled. "Everyone have an awesome 2006!" They didn't kick us out. They didn't even lock the doors. We were all technically trespassing, keeping the ghost of that coffee house alive as a massive, unhinged party. Mojo's is gone now, but absolutely no one who was there will _ever_ forget the night it closed its doors and dragged us kicking and screaming into 2006. Mushuto crossed over himself in 2007, then Supa left us years later. But the music? The music lives on. Legends never really die. ## Apocalypse -- The Beginning This is it -- the final retrospective on '05 and the beautiful, reckless chaos that bled directly into the album. This is what brought us to this door and to the original album itself. ### Burning Man: The Psyche My very first burn. It gave me a desperate shot of hope for humanity. Out of five years spent hitchhiking the globe, it was the absolute first time I'd ever felt actual "homesickness" for a physical place. Walking out of that dust, the compass shifted: I knew I had to evolve from just DJing to full-on production. Just weeks later, that exact drive slammed me right into Mushuto. ### Set Adrift Throughout '05, I was a ghost bouncing between The Demon Den (Mephie's place -- and holy hell, did we defile that room!), Gaea's, Loki's, my gig at Thundercloud, MeMe's, and occasionally just roughing it out on the streets. All of it was just pressure building up to hitting the open road and hitching again in '06. Then, as I laid out earlier, I ended the year literally living out of Mojo's Coffee before they killed the lights for good on NYE. ### The Love Spiderweb The year kicked off with Pandora keeping me as her literal and willing pet. From there, it spun out into PJ, Gallows, Nathan, a little bit of Dallas... and, naturally, heavy splashes of Kaycee and her signature chaos. It was one hell of a tangled web. Despite the street rumors, Faerie and Xoltan weren't actually caught in the netting -- though we definitely didn't lift a finger to kill the gossip. Post-burn, I brutally severed the cords, ripping myself out of the web to forcefully reclaim my energy and to hyper-focus entirely on the art and the music. ### The Art Scene I locked down the final third of the holy trinity of DJ sets that started back in 2001 with "Tears of Ra" and continued through 2003 with "[Blood of the Moon](blood-of-the-moon)." I finally closed the book with "Shadows of Twilight." On top of that, I dropped three _[ADHD Revolution](adhd-revolution)_ sets. It was a massive, blood-letting year for music, with me cutting a lot of those mixes live straight from the floor at Mojo's. Every single ounce of this madness went into the music... and spilled over into the years that followed. _Every. damn. inch._

texts:
### Extended Exploration

Fans of "IO Limiters" will love "[IO Vapoura](io-vapoura)" from the same series, which will also be seeing a 20-year anniversary edition. The story leads visually into my [surreal fractalscapes](other-fractalscapes) series of designs.
